After 2 h incubation in a cell culture incubator the imaging chamber was transferred to the microscope kept at 37 °C and 5% CO2.

Here we present an experimental and image-processing framework capable of turning long-term light-sheet imaging of intestinal organoids into digital organoids. The framework combines specific imaging optimization combined with data processing via deep learning techniques to segment single organoids, their lumen, cells and nuclei in 3D over long periods of time.

specimen.growth_conditions: Mouse small-intestinal organoids maintained in IntestiCult Organoid Growth Medium (STEM CELL Technologies) with 100 µg/ml Penicillin-Streptomycin. For light-sheet imaging, FACS-sorted single cells were collected in ENR medium (advanced DMEM/F-12 with 15 mM HEPES (STEM CELL Technologies), 100 µg/ml Penicillin-Streptomycin, 1x Glutamax, 1x B27, 1x N2 (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 1 mM N-acetylcysteine (Sigma), 500 ng/ml R-Spondin, 100 ng/ml Noggin (PeproTech), 100 ng/ml murine EGF (R&D Systems)); 2500 cells were embedded in a 5 µl drop of Matrigel/medium at a 60/40 ratio. For the first 3 days the medium was supplemented with 20% Wnt3a-conditioned medium and 10 µM Y-27632 (ROCK inhibitor), and on the first day additionally with 3 µM CHIR99021. Medium was exchanged manually every day during acquisition.

study.dataset_name: Liberali Lab LS1 Time-Lapse Organoid Dataset
study.description: Live 3D light-sheet time-lapse recordings of mouse intestinal organoids from the Liberali lab. Each store is one cropped organoid ROI, imaged in two fluorescence channels (mem9-GFP plasma membrane, H2B-mCherry nuclei) at 10-minute intervals over several hundred timepoints. Every ROI is provided in three processing variants — raw, deconvolved and denoised. The deconvolved store additionally carries cell, nuclei and lumen segmentation masks, single-cell tracking converted to GEFF, VTP surface meshes, and per-cell and organoid-level feature tables.
